fields.title: The Inescapable Triangle
fields.keyTakeaway: The model is chosen from sufficient quality to minimum price, and not the other way around, and a quality gain of a few percentage points rarely justifies a multiplier in cost and latency.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Why can't we just take the best model?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The choice of model determines product quality, unit cost, and speed all at once. A decision made on one criterion worsens the other two, and this becomes apparent at scale.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[quality-cost-latency-triangle|Three quantities are linked]]: stronger model — better quality, higher price, more latency. You cannot bypass this, you can only choose a point.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: The last row requires explanation: reasoning models spend extra tokens on internal thinking before answering. Quality on complex tasks is higher, but we pay with both time and tokens that the user does not see. Excessive for most product scenarios.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/items/0: **Determine what quality is sufficient.** Not "maximum", but the threshold where the feature is useful. Determined by evals and product metrics.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/items/1: **Find the cheapest model that provides this threshold.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/items/2: **Check latency.** If it doesn't fit — either another model or a UI change.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: The reverse order — taking a flagship and then trimming — yields a product whose economics don't work out, and no one knows how much it could have been trimmed.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: A separate consideration: **different parts of a feature require different things.** Covered in `AI2-N3-L2`. A flagship model is rarely needed and only on a narrow step.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/0/2: Simple task, speed and price matter
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/2/2: Small lost 14% factual accuracy per evals
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/3/2: Tested flagship — 3% gain at 6x the price
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/4/2: Structural task, result verified by code
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Testing the flagship model on cart recommendation is a telling case. Quality gain per evals was 3%, cost was 6 times higher, latency was twice as high. Product-wise, 3% is indistinguishable from noise, and 7.8 seconds would turn into 15. We rejected it.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Reasoning models were tried on one task: "explain why this set is more expensive than usual". Quality of explanations noticeably better, latency 22 seconds. For a feature used by 2%, unacceptable. We solved it differently: the explanation is prepared not by the model, but by a calculation with a template.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Tier boundaries are blurring, prices are dropping, and a model that was flagship falls into the medium tier by price a year later. Re-evaluating the choice is worth doing once a quarter.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: The model is chosen from sufficient quality to minimum price, and not the other way around, and a quality gain of a few percentage points rarely justifies a multiplier in cost and latency.
